summary: Signed Walsh-Hadamard rotation for low-bit KV storage; preserves unquantized attention algebra, while quantization error can improve or worsen
implementation_scope: FP64 Python rotation (signed normalized Walsh-Hadamard), symmetric per-32 int8/int4 quantization and rotated versus unrotated attention comparison; reference CUDA rotate-quantize, rotate, unrotate and dequantize kernels for power-of-two head dimensions 32-1024. Attention kernels, int4 packing and cache layout are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: The KV cache is stored as low-bit integers with per-group scales and some channels are much larger than others
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The cache stays in BF16/FP16, or channel magnitudes are already even
provides: R = H * diag(signs) with deterministic signs, its inverse and the score/output identities
Symmetric per-32 quantization at 4 or 8 bits with ties to even
Rotated versus unrotated attention comparison on the host
Reference CUDA rotate-quantize, query rotate, output unrotate and dequantize kernels
engine_supplies: Rotation placement after position encoding and key normalization
Attention reading dequantized stored rows and unrotating (or folding R^T into) the output
Int4 packing, cache layout and the representation key with seed, dimension, bits and group
Model-quality measurement against the unquantized cache and an unrotated cache at the same bit width/group size
preserve: Queries, keys, values and outputs share the same rotation
The rotation is part of the cache representation identity
Codes are symmetric with one FP32 scale per 32 values
adapt: Seed, group size and bit width
Folding R or R^T into adjacent projections
Fusing rotate-quantize into append and dequantization into attention

code_files.purpose: FP64 rotation, group quantization and rotated/unrotated attention comparison
CUDA launch interface for rotate-quantize, rotate, unrotate and dequantize
Reference one-block-per-row kernels with a shared-memory Walsh-Hadamard transform, not for performance

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library; CUDA C++20 with Core CRIT_CORE_CUDA for the device reference
requires.model: Attention heads with a power-of-two head dimension from 32 to 1024
requires.workload: Low-bit KV storage where memory matters more than the per-row transform cost

contract.input: Key, value and query rows with a stride, the sign vector, and 4 or 8 bits
contract.output: Int8 codes and per-32 FP32 scales of rotated rows; rotated queries; unrotated outputs; dequantized stored rows
contract.ownership: The engine owns rows, signs, codes, scales and outputs; kernels borrow them on the caller stream
contract.failure: Reject null pointers, non-power-of-two or out-of-range dimensions, short strides and bit widths other than 4 or 8
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; KV representation and attention remain engine choices

dependencies: CUDA runtime for the device reference

validation.host: Transform self-inverse, dot-product preservation, sign determinism, group quantization bounds, invalid input, lower attention error on a fixed outlier-channel int8 fixture, and sparse/constant int4 counterexamples where rotation increases error
validation.native: CUDA rows of dimension 128 with outlier channels against FP64: rotation, inverse, in-place rotation, codes within half a step, rejected launches and lower rotated than unrotated int8 attention error
